rv.q: Unlike a typical episode of Black Mirror, the Experience lacks sharp satirical bite or deep philosophical insight.

The proceedings have the veneer of a Black Mirror episode, and there are a few truly disturbing images, but the premise didn’t blow my mind like the best episodes of the show have, or even leave me with much to chew on.

There are a handful of moments in which its fractured reflection of our reality is intriguingly put to use in The Black Mirror Experience, but as a whole, it isn’t consistent or polished enough to necessarily warrant signing away your data (if only for a few weeks) to another thing.
It’s a technically impressive and diverting lark that combines elements of dystopian video game, escape room, and interactive theme park ride.

cn.t: This technically impressive VR-meets-escape room hybrid offers a diverting if gimmicky dive into Black Mirror's dystopian world, though critics find it more novelty than substance.
